witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 64.6a
div.ab: Si secus sit, semper erit possidens propior quam repetens et habeat; aut ille, si potest, [c]enninga resistat, que ultra terciam uicem non procedit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 584 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Gewährzug. Vgl. Très anc. cout. Norm. II 82: Tenens potest nominare garantum . . . . Et si tercius nominauerit quartum, oportet quod statim causam defendat, quia nominatio garantorum non procedit ulterius

Vouching to warranty. Cf. Très anc. cout. Norm. II 82: Tenens potest nominare garantum . . . . Et si tercius nominauerit quartum, oportet quod statim causam defendat, quia nominatio garantorum non procedit ulterius

div.ab: If it is otherwise, the possessor shall always be nearer than the claimant, and let him have it; or let that man, if he can, resist by cenninga (declaration of warranty), which does not go beyond the third time.
